analysis.title: Oracle: AI World 2026 strikes the right tone
key_insights: DB reiterates Buy and $300 price target on Oracle (ORCL) after AI World and the financial-analyst meeting. Thesis: AI Infrastructure backlog becomes a highly value-creative business over time, complementary to Core OCI, Cloud DB and Applications.
Management reiterated FY30 targets of $225bn revenue and $21 EPS, in line with DB's expectations going in.

Management gave more clarity on funding: the remaining FY27 capital plan is $20bn (excluding refinancing), below what most expected, split 50% debt and 50% equity. No incremental capital raises are envisioned through FY30 after that.

Upfront CapEx through FY28 is cut by about 50%, using prepayments, vendor financing and BYOHW (bring-your-own-hardware) agreements that sound already secured. After FY28 the business is expected to self-fund from cash flow.

Oracle expects positive FCF by F2H28 and $30bn+ FCF by FY29. Prior consensus expected negative annual FCF until FY30. DB says this removes a key overhang and shifts focus past the FY27/28 peak investment phase to the FY30 targets.
Very limited infrastructure capacity is left to contract through FY28. Focus shifts to execution on the 7GW+ build-out and conversion of $664bn+ of RPO backlog.
Oracle plans to add 7GW of new capacity over FY27/28, bringing the total footprint to 10GW. About half comes from large gigawatt-scale sites and the rest from its 200+ region global footprint.

Oracle will be the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer Google TPUs, starting in 2027 and reaching GW scale in the coming years. It is also adding OpenAI Jalapeño, Cerebras, Positron Atlas and SambaNova SN50 inference accelerators to OCI.

NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs are generally available on OCI, with plans for multi-gigawatt expansion. New partnerships include a native NetApp Storage Service and Snowflake as a native first-party service.

Cloud Database growth has decelerated for two quarters to +26% y/y at constant currency in F1Q. Multi-cloud grew 353% y/y in F1Q off a small base. CFO Hilary Maxson again called for Cloud Database growth 'well in excess of 50%', which DB sees as consistent with the $20bn FY30 AI Database + AI Data Platform target.

DB says it is too early to see the Deep Trust AI Architecture and AI Data Platform show up in financial results, and it has not come up in DB's customer or partner conversations. Oracle faces competition in data platforms from Snowflake, Databricks, Palantir and the CSPs.

Oracle announced 25 Fusion Agentic Applications powered by Fusion Claw across ERP, HCM, SCM and CX. Fusion adoption stats: 7k customers using Fusion AI/Agents, 150m+ Fusion tool calls in F1Q, 500bn tokens in September. DB does not expect a real commercial impact from consumption-based AI-unit pricing until at least FY28.

Management said new agent-based automation can shorten Fusion implementations by 50-80% and reiterated a ~3x revenue uplift on on-prem-to-cloud migrations. Migrations and cross-sell are key levers for double-digit SaaS growth.

The OpenAI relationship expands into enterprise software: Oracle AI Workspace, Oracle App Composer (Codex), Oracle AI Security Mesh and an AI Services Practice powered by OpenAI. Oracle has not disclosed the economics, so DB says the financial impact is hard to quantify.
Watch items: NGOM (guided to 40% in FY30, expected down near-term on capacity ramps), project delays, data points on largest customer OpenAI, and Oracle's long-term share in AI infrastructure.

market_movers.rationale: Funding need of $20bn is below expectations, FCF turns positive in F2H28, and the full-stack AI case was well laid out. Shares closed at $144.54 on 28 Oct 26, against a 52-week range of 114.99 to 278.66.

sector_views.rationale: DB rates Oracle Buy on the AI infrastructure backlog and full-stack enterprise AI position. No broader sector call is made in the note.

earnings_insights: No new quarterly print in this note. Cloud Database growth was +26% y/y at constant currency in F1Q (reported), decelerating for the past two quarters. Multi-cloud grew 353% y/y in F1Q.
Management targets (not estimates): FY30 revenue $225bn, FY30 EPS $21, FY30 NGOM 40%, FCF positive from F2H28, $30bn+ FCF by FY29. Prior consensus expected negative annual FCF until FY30.
risk_factors: Execution risk on the 7GW+ build-out and project delays.
NGOM is expected to fall near-term on the pace of capacity ramps before recovering toward the 40% FY30 guide.
Dependence on largest customer OpenAI and uncertainty over its performance.
Cloud Database growth has decelerated to +26% y/y at cc, below the 'well in excess of 50%' needed for long-term EPS targets.
Competition in the data-platform market from Snowflake, Databricks, Palantir and the CSPs.
The economics of the OpenAI product partnerships are undisclosed.
Funding relies on a 50/50 debt and equity mix, and the financing models do not themselves necessarily raise project NPV.

tension_points.bull_case: Funding need is only $20bn, split 50/50 debt and equity, with FCF positive from F2H28 and $30bn+ FCF by FY29, removing the key overhang and refocusing on FY30 targets.
tension_points.bear_case: Financing models do not necessarily enhance project NPV. Execution on the 7GW+ build-out, NGOM dilution near-term, Cloud Database deceleration to +26% and reliance on OpenAI remain risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Project delays, NGOM falling below the path to 40% in FY30, or Cloud Database growth failing to inflect toward 'well in excess of 50%'.

theme_stances.key_argument: Lower funding needs and an earlier return to positive FCF remove a key overhang on the stock.
theme_stances.evidence: well below the capital needs most had been expecting

theme_stances.key_argument: An inflection in Cloud Database growth is key to hitting long-term EPS targets, but it is too early to see it in results.
theme_stances.evidence: it still appears too early to see if this shows up
